findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The semantic skill-integrity check in `asset-integrity.ts` is narrow and sound. It only applies to `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and only when the inventory carries a valid 64-hex `skill_sha256`. Under the YAML 1.2 core schema it rejects: - duplicate keys, - aliases, - unknown tags, - non-string keys, - non-finite numbers, - invalid UTF-8.  Mapping keys are sorted deterministically by code unit, and `JSON.stringify([metadata, body])` encodes the metadata and body without ambiguity. The body after the front matter is compared byte for byte. Runtime and template assets stay byte-exact, and older inventories without the semantic digest stay strict.  The unit tests distinguish the important cases: - a boolean versus the quoted string `"true"`, - a reordered sequence, - an added key, - a one-byte body change, - CRLF versus LF line endings, - a trailing-newline change.  The wiring is proven through real collaborators. The dispatcher and profile-observation tests copy the real generated `plugin/` directory, normalize `skills/audit/SKILL.md`, and assert: - normalized metadata is accepted, - changed metadata, body, or runtime is rejected, - malformed metadata is rejected with the 'Skill front matter is invalid' diagnostic.  This also shows the shipped inventory includes `skill_sha256` for that skill. The remaining concerns are residual risks, not demonstrated failures.

`asset-integrity.ts` treats two headers as equal if they parse the same under the `yaml` package's 1.2 core schema. Claude may read front matter with a different parser or schema. Example: unquoted `2024-01-01` is a string under core 1.2 but a Date under YAML 1.1 parsers such as js-yaml's default schema. If desktop sync ever quotes or unquotes such a scalar, the meaning Claude sees could change while the hash still matches. This can only be triggered by whatever rewrites the cache (desktop sync or an actor already inside the cache trust boundary), so it is non-blocking. Consider documenting which parser Claude uses, or rejecting scalars that YAML 1.1 and 1.2 would read differently.

`canonicalValue` turns YAML integers into JS numbers. Integers beyond 2^53 (e.g. `12345678901234567890` and `12345678901234567891`) can therefore produce the same hash. Skill metadata is unlikely to hold such values, but a stricter check would reject unsafe integers (`Number.isSafeInteger` for integer nodes) or parse with `intAsBigInt`.

The desktop-normalization tests use `yaml.stringify(parse(...))` as a stand-in for what desktop sync actually does (#6004). If the real sync also changes bytes outside the header, the skill will still be reported as a damaged cache: adding a BOM, changing the blank line after the closing `---`, or converting body line endings to CRLF. That fails closed, so it is not a security problem, but the fix may not fully cover the reported issue. A captured real desktop-rewritten fixture would make the proof stronger.

In `dispatch.test.ts`, the `'body'` case of the mutation switch has a redundant nested block containing a stray `// No default` comment, and `'malformed-metadata'` has an extra blank line. These look like lint auto-fix leftovers. Behavior is correct, but they hurt readability. Flatten the block and add an explicit `'runtime'`/`default` arm.

`verifyInventoryAsset` in the dispatcher (context only) still hashes every asset a second time just to build the diagnostic message, even when validation passes. This is ledger item R2, which is still open; it costs performance, not correctness.

Line-ending changes on the `---` delimiter lines themselves (LF vs CRLF after the opening or closing marker) are excluded from the semantic hash. CRLF in the body is still rejected. These newlines carry no meaning, so this is acceptable, but it is a deliberate gap in byte coverage.

The code that generates `inventory.json` and emits `skill_sha256` is not in this packet. Its correctness is inferred from the end-to-end tests against the real `plugin/` directory, which cover only `skills/audit`. A generator-level check that every `skills/*/SKILL.md` entry gets a `skill_sha256` would close that gap.
